record_envelope.rule: Every research record in every layer carries the envelope fields; definition_refs bind the release bundle active at submission time.

consumption.usable_basis: For each work/source: the latest active revision whose content_state='stable' (stable requires passed structural validation and independent agent review approval).
consumption.current_revision: The latest active revision regardless of content state; always visible next to the usable basis.
consumption.human_adoption_role: Human adoption remains an independent human judgment overlay (R04); it is never required for research consumption, comparison, citation or export (R07/U3).
consumption.three_states: needs_completion/needs_review/stable are content states of records; they are independent of human reading status and are never bulk-upgraded by migration.
consumption.unread_materials: Unread or human-pending materials keep participating in queries, comparison, citation and candidate analysis.

task_protocol.task_package: A task package binds environment_id, batch_id, plan_digest, the active release bundle, per-item source/snapshot bindings and the submission/receipt/error contract for one external worker.
task_protocol.receipts: Every mutating operation accepts an operation_id; the first durable outcome is stored as an idempotent receipt and replays identically for retries.
task_protocol.expected_head_id: A worker may pin expected_head_id; a mismatch with the current head yields revision_conflict instead of a silent fork.
task_protocol.lease: Worker mutations require worker_owner + attempt fencing while the lease is unexpired; offline mutations require manual_action with an explicit reason and audit event.

human_readable_output.rule: Agent- or model-authored human-readable explanatory content defaults to Chinese.

invariants: Every record binds an explicit source_file_id, parse_run_id, snapshot_id and snapshot_sha256.
Every distinct parse_run_id retains its own snapshot binding and parse quality even when its text content hash is identical to another run.
A source can have multiple globally unique citation aliases without changing its preserved work_id or source_file_id.
Every claim has at least one exact evidence anchor in the bound immutable text snapshot.
Successful structural and evidence-anchor validation is recorded independently as validation_status=passed on both record layers.
Agent review and human adoption are independent state transitions; neither implies the other.
A canonical plan_digest binds every request_key to its name, ontology version, contract version and sorted source/snapshot pairs; different intent conflicts unless an explicit rerun is requested.

A batch item records worker ownership, heartbeat/lease timestamps, a monotonically increasing attempt fencing token and durable recovery metadata; a crashed running item is reclaimed only by an explicit recover-running action.
Worker submission and failure mutations require the current owner and attempt token while the lease is unexpired; offline mutations require an explicit manual_action flag, reason and audit event.
A batch item remains running after source-record submission and becomes submitted only after its interpretation is stored; failed items retain an error and can be retried explicitly.
An identical record retry is idempotent; non-identical content requires an explicit supersedes_id that is the current linear head and creates a new version.

An interpretation can only bind the active source-record head selected by its batch item; consumption additionally requires that interpretation itself to be structurally valid and independently reviewed.
Legacy analysis and approval rows are never selected by research-workflow queries.
Ontology publication transactionally recomputes its base-version impact set and invalidates all currently active dependent interpretations, never source snapshots or source records.
Ordinary Agent review never clears ontology impact; only proposal-specific approval of a new relabel revision can clear that proposal's re-review requirement.
Legacy validation_status, agent_review_status and human_adoption_status query filters are compatibility aliases for the interpretation layer only.

Agent- or model-authored explanatory content defaults to Chinese, while stable identifiers, schema keys, enum internal values, proper names, exact source quotes, evidence offsets and locators remain verbatim.
A Chinese display adaptation of a reviewed record is an independently versioned, exactly bound, display-only artifact; it never mutates the reviewed payload or inherits review/adoption status.

A definition release is an immutable bundle of one definition version per layer (metadata, source_record, interpretation, ontology) with content hashes; released definitions never change in place and are retired only by a new release.
Record submissions bind the definition_refs of one release bundle; validation checks payloads against the bound definitions (incompatible_definition otherwise).

content_state transitions are: submissions start at needs_completion or needs_review; only passed structural validation plus independent agent review approval moves a record to stable; supersede/retraction returns revisions to needs_review; human actions never set stable directly.
Migration never marks migrated records stable; it assigns needs_review (or needs_completion when structural validation or evidence is incomplete) and preserves every prior state column.
A formal revision created from feedback records the feedback_id; feedback outcomes are corrected, partially_corrected, retained_with_evidence or unresolved, and pages/exports echo the outcome.

Citation edges (cites) require a verified evidence anchor in the citing work's bound snapshot; unresolved identity stays a candidate/unmatched reference object and never silently binds an existing work.
Cross-paper exports separate usable-basis content from current candidates and never present candidates as stable conclusions.
Receipts are idempotent by operation_id; a replayed operation returns the original durable outcome without re-executing.
Task packages carry an explicit environment_id; a package is only valid against the environment that issued it.
